raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Qwen3CoderDetector` (parsers `qwen3_coder`, `step3p5`, `nanbeige`) finds tool calls in `detect_and_parse` with `re.compile(r"<tool_call>(.*?)</tool_call>", re.DOTALL).findall(text)`. When `</tool_call>` never arrives, each opening tag rescans to the end of the text, so the cost is quadratic. On the fuzzer-found inputs this `findall` accounted for all of the time: nanbeige 3.2 s at 70 KB, qwen3_coder 2.4 s at 56 KB, step3p5 0.85 s at 36 KB.

| Input (repeated `<tool_call> `) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 23 KB | 0.36 s | 0.1 ms |
| 46 KB | 1.4 s | 0.1 ms |
| 93 KB | 5.8 s | 0.2 ms |

Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- `_iter_tool_call_bodies`: a linear `str.find` scan yielding exactly the bodies `findall` returned. The now-unused `tool_call_regex` attribute is removed. The fallback for text with no complete block is unchanged.
- Regression test `TestQwen3CoderDetector::test_unclosed_tool_call_tags_parse_in_linear_time`: 56.2 s on `main`, fast here.

## Accuracy Tests

- Differential test of `main` vs patched detector, comparing `detect_and_parse` and every streaming result under random re-chunking: **0 mismatches** over 20k random plus 20k mutated well-formed inputs (18.7k produced parsed calls).
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/`: 630 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above. A scaling probe (each token literal and each pair, repeated 2k/4k/8k times) finds no remaining super-linear input. The function and parameter regexes that run afterwards measured linear.

Related: #42573, #42574, #42575, #42576, #42577, #42578 (same issue class in other tool-call parsers).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -32,7 +32,6 @@ def __init__(self):
         self.parameter_end_token: str = "</parameter>"
 
         # Regex for non-streaming fallback
-        self.tool_call_regex = re.compile(r"<tool_call>(.*?)</tool_call>", re.DOTALL)
         self.tool_call_function_regex = re.compile(
             r"<function=(.*?)</function>|<function=(.*)$", re.DOTALL
         )
@@ -61,6 +60,20 @@ def __init__(self):
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         return self.tool_call_start_token in text
 
+    def _iter_tool_call_bodies(self, text: str):
+        # Linear scan on purpose: a `<tool_call>(.*?)</tool_call>` findall rescans
+        # to the end from every opening tag when the end tag never arrives.
+        start = text.find(self.tool_call_start_token)
+        while start != -1:
+            body_start = start + len(self.tool_call_start_token)
+            end = text.find(self.tool_call_end_token, body_start)
+            if end == -1:
+                return
+            yield text[body_start:end]
+            start = text.find(
+                self.tool_call_start_token, end + len(self.tool_call_end_token)
+            )
+
     def _get_arguments_config(
         self, func_name: str, tools: Optional[list[Tool]]
     ) -> dict:
@@ -184,7 +197,7 @@ def detect_and_parse(self, text: str, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult
         try:
             # Simple cleanup of the text to find tool calls
             # Note: This is a simplified regex approach consistent with vLLM
-            raw_tool_calls = self.tool_call_regex.findall(text)
+            raw_tool_calls = list(self._iter_tool_call_bodies(text))
             if not raw_tool_calls:
                 # Fallback: maybe the whole text is inside the tag or tags are stripped
                 if self.tool_call_prefix in text:

@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 import functools
 import json
+import time
 import unittest
 import warnings
 
@@ -2262,6 +2263,26 @@ def test_multiple_tool_calls(self):
         self.assertEqual(params2["query"], "SELECT * FROM users")
         self.assertEqual(params2["dry_run"], True)
 
+    def test_unclosed_tool_call_tags_parse_in_linear_time(self):
+        """Many opening tags without a closing tag must not stall the parser
+        (it runs on the event loop); earlier complete calls still parse."""
+        text = (
+            "<tool_call>\n<function=get_current_weather>\n"
+            "<parameter=location>New York</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"
+            + "<tool_call> "
+            * 25000
+        )
+
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        result = self.detector.detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+
+        self.assertLess(elapsed, 1.0)
+        self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters), {"location": "New York"}
+        )
+
